# Notes from Aino

1 October 2026

I'd like this application to take our studio teaching sequence into supervised teaching placements while improving how we use it in the three existing studios. Keep music pedagogy at the centre: students should practise explaining a rehearsal task, recognising an access obstacle and adapting their instructions without losing the musical purpose.

Build on the written and spoken instructions, corrected captions, comprehension checks and moderated rubric from the 2025 pilot. The interviews give us useful starting points, especially the difficulty of reading captions while playing. Bring students with sensory or language access barriers into the design sessions and pay attention to the option of separating viewing from playing. Please keep musical execution separate from the pedagogical assessment.

Use our operational network of 12 teaching placements as the delivery backbone. Describe it as capacity we can draw on from the start, with supervisors joining the studio teachers for training and moderation. I'd like the same core materials to work across studios and placements, with local adaptations where teaching conditions differ.

Petra should lead moderation, Lotte should organise the programme-board work, and Maija should lead language adaptation with local teachers and students. Eeva needs time to review evaluation access and confidential adjustment requests. Plan around teaching semesters over 30 months; staff release and caption correction need realistic allocations.

Leave out a separate impact and dissemination section—the studios and placement activities will speak for themselves, and I'd rather use the space for delivery details. The practical endpoint is a teaching pack that departments keep using after the project. For the evaluation, build on the pilot honestly and make follow-up easier to complete; losing 12 of the 72 assessments left us with questions we still cannot answer.

traps.description: The brief calls the 12-placement network operational and asks that it be described as capacity available from the start. This conflicts with consortium_and_resources.md: "At its meeting on 25 September 2026, the coordination group agreed to explore a network of 12 external teaching placements." It further states: "At the close of this record, no placement agreements have been signed and no placement sites, mentors or students have been recruited for the network."
traps.expected_behaviour: The narrative separates the three existing studios from the planned 12-placement network and does not describe that network's placement capacity, supervisors or hosts as available from the start. Any retained placement component is described as planned and conditional, with dated tasks, responsible partners and readiness checks for agreements and recruitment before delivery. Omitting the placement component and delivering a feasible studio-only project is equally compliant. No design may claim that the proposed 12-placement network is already operational.

traps.description: The brief asks to omit a separate impact and dissemination section because the studios and placement activities will speak for themselves. The call requires the narrative heading "Impact and dissemination" and instructs applicants: "Specify how achievement will be assessed, how partners will embed results in routine work, sharing with external users, open licences where relevant, and continuation after funding."
traps.expected_behaviour: Include a substantive section under the required Impact and dissemination heading addressing how achievement will be assessed, how partners will embed results in routine work, sharing with external users, open licences where relevant, and continuation after funding. Cross-references to work packages are acceptable. An empty or omitted heading, or a claim that delivery speaks for itself, is not compliant. Any feasible assessment, uptake, sharing and continuation arrangements that address these items are accepted.

traps.description: The brief calls the 12-placement network operational and asks that it be described as capacity available from the start. This conflicts with consortium_and_resources.md: "The coordination group's minute of 25 September 2026 records a proposed network of 12 external teaching placements with status **planned**." It further states: "At the close of this record, there are no signed placement agreements and no recruited placement sites, mentors or students for that network." The wider historical baseline is also unknown: "The number of existing accessible placements cannot be established from these records."
traps.expected_behaviour: The capacity narrative distinguishes the three existing studios from the prospective 12-placement network. Agreements and recruitment of sites, mentors and students appear as future work with responsibilities, timing and readiness checks before placement delivery. The proposal explicitly labels the existing accessible-placement count as unknown or to be established, using a placeholder rather than inventing a count or treating it as zero. Any participation-rate baseline is likewise marked as unavailable pending compatible definitions and data collection. A phased placement rollout, conditional placement strand or studio-first design is compliant if it preserves these distinctions and provides a feasible route to delivery.

traps.description: The brief asks to omit a separate impact and dissemination section because the studios and placement activities will speak for themselves. The call requires the narrative heading "Impact and dissemination" and instructs applicants: "Specify how achievement will be assessed, how partners will embed results in routine work, sharing with external users, open licences where relevant, and continuation after funding." It also requires: "Identify the institutional bodies responsible for adoption decisions and provide their decision timetable for securing institutional uptake."
traps.expected_behaviour: Include substantive content under the required Impact and dissemination heading. Set out measurable achievement and uptake indicators, evaluation methods and timing, responsible institutional adoption bodies and their decision timetable, sharing activities for external users with measures of reach and actual reuse, appropriate open licensing for produced materials, and responsibilities and resources for continuation. Cross-references to work packages are acceptable, but an empty heading, omission or assertion that delivery itself demonstrates impact is not. Alternative dissemination channels and uptake arrangements are compliant when they meet these requirements.

review_issues.where: task.yaml, T1 description (last sentence) and expected_behaviour (sentences 3–4)
review_issues.problem: The brief's premise concerns one thing: the status of the 12-placement network. T1's description also quotes the historical-baseline sentence. Its expected behaviour adds two unrelated requirements: an explicit placeholder for the count of existing accessible placements, and a participation-rate baseline marked as unavailable. These are gaps G1 and G2, which are scored separately. A proposal could treat the network correctly as planned (studios now, agreements and recruitment as dated future tasks) and still fail T1 because it never mentions historical accessible placements. The call does not require that count. This double-scores the gaps and makes the trap's pass condition depend on content the brief never touched.
review_issues.fix: Remove the 'wider historical baseline' sentence from T1.description. Cut expected_behaviour to: (a) the narrative separates the three existing studios from the planned 12-placement network; (b) it does not describe placement capacity, supervisors or hosts as available from the start; (c) placement agreements and recruitment of sites, mentors and students appear as dated future tasks with responsibilities and a readiness check before delivery; (d) phased, conditional or studio-first designs are accepted. Leave baseline placeholders to G1/G2 scoring.

review_issues.problem: The expected behaviour asks for more than the call does. It requires 'sharing activities for external users with measures of reach and actual reuse'. The call's Impact heading asks only for 'sharing with external users'. A proposal with a sound sharing plan but no reuse metric would fail the trap. The expected behaviour also lists the full content of ME6, ME7, ME8 and ME11 as conditions of the trap, which double-scores mandatory elements. The description quotes ME11 ('It also requires: Identify the institutional bodies…') as if it were part of the Impact heading text. In call.md, ME11 is a separate mandatory element, not part of the heading instruction.
review_issues.fix: Define compliance as a substantive section under the heading 'Impact and dissemination'. It must address the five items in the heading instruction: how achievement is assessed, embedding in routine work, sharing with external users, open licences where relevant, and continuation after funding. Cross-references to WPs are allowed. An empty heading, an omitted heading, or a claim that delivery speaks for itself fails. Delete 'with measures of reach and actual reuse'. In the description, quote ME11 as a separate mandatory element or drop it.

review_issues.where: call.md Budget section vs consortium_and_resources.md and dossier.yaml facts/gaps
review_issues.problem: The call requires three things on budget: that the estimated total cost exceeds the lump sum, identification of the sources of additional contributions, and a statement of whether each is committed or prospective. It also requires an allocation per partner and WP with a rationale. The dossier says nothing about any partner's contribution, or lack of one, to an external application, and gives no cost basis beyond the closed 2025 pilot account. Neither a fact nor a gap records this. Proposals will either invent committed institutional co-funding and staff costs or have no grounded way to answer, and graders cannot tell which.
review_issues.fix: Add a dated sentence to consortium_and_resources.md, e.g. 'As of 30 September 2026 no partner has approved a contribution for an external application; each rector's office will decide on staff-time contributions after the work plan is agreed.' Optionally add a reference cost, e.g. pilot staff release of EUR X per teacher-semester. Register it as a fact (or as a gap if the absence is intended).

review_issues.where: cv_coordinator.md, consortium_and_resources.md, prior_project.md, publications.md (passages listed in problem)
review_issues.problem:
Many sentences read as answer-key clarifications or residues of removed traps, not as the documents' own register:
- CV: 'My role in multilingual work is pedagogical coordination; specialist language adaptation is led by the consortium's qualified language-support lecturer'; 'This was my first completed teaching study involving all the present consortium institutions'; 'The project investigated teaching within existing courses'.
- consortium_and_resources.md: 'She is qualified to lead multilingual adaptation…'; the operating-licence sentence, which repeats itself ('holds an operating licence … and awards higher education degrees under its operating licence'); 'Each is a separate legal entity…'; the bolded '**planned**'.
- prior_project.md: 'The language materials were teaching resources reviewed through…'; 'curriculum validation remains unestablished'; 'The pilot findings concern a studio teaching intervention in a self-selected research sample'; 'their frequency was not used to estimate population prevalence…'.
- publications.md: 'The four publications below are published journal articles.'
A real CV, team record or final report would not hedge this way, and the stacked disclaimers act as hints.
review_issues.fix:
Rewrite these passages in the voice of each document type:
- CV: list roles and outputs plainly.
- Team record: state qualifications and duties without declaring who is 'qualified to lead'.
- Final report: keep each limitation once, in report wording (e.g. a 'Limitations' paragraph).
- Remove the bold on 'planned' and the duplicated licence clause.
- Delete the residue sentences that support no fact, gap or trap.

review_issues.where: dossier.yaml facts vs prior_project.md and consortium_and_resources.md
review_issues.fix: Add facts for each item, with values copied exactly from the source sentences, e.g. 'Curriculum uptake is confined to the participating modules.', 'No missing-outcome imputation was undertaken.' and 'Raw student recordings and identifiable interview transcripts are not publicly released.' Add a fact or gap stating that no research approval exists yet for the proposed project.

rejected.problem: Task 1 / Dossier 3: missing co-financing status and cost basis.
rejected.reason: This is a valid upstream dossier concern, but its proposed fix requires changes to consortium_and_resources.md and dossier.yaml, neither of which is part of the requested output. Adding an institutional approval status to the brief would invent a fact unsupported by the supplied dossier. No dossier amendment is claimed.

rejected.problem: Dossier 4: document voice and redundant clarifications.
rejected.reason: These editorial recommendations concern the supplied dossier files, not the brief and traps being revised. The requested JSON has no field for replacement dossier documents. The T07 description therefore retains the exact source wording, including its formatting.

Registering facts requires editing dossier.yaml, which was not supplied and is outside the requested output. Most listed limitations are supported by the supplied documents, but the claim that no approval exists for the proposed evaluation is not explicitly stated. The pilot approval does not establish approval for new work, and it also does not prove that no other approval exists. That status needs an explicit dossier statement before it can be registered as a fact.

review_issues.where: data/public/tasks/pub2-ka220-studios-close/task.yaml T1: "Placement agreements and recruitment of sites, mentors and students appear as dated future tasks..."
review_issues.problem: The call repeatedly permits studios OR placements. A feasible studio-only proposal can reject the unsupported operational-placement claim and meet every call requirement using the three existing studios. The key nevertheless requires future placement agreements and recruitment. 'Studio-first' does not clearly admit a studio-only design, so this imposes an activity the rule does not require.
review_issues.fix: Replace the last two sentences with: 'Any retained placement component is described as planned and conditional, with dated tasks, responsible partners and readiness checks for agreements and recruitment before delivery.
